newsitem.title: USA: Free markets best route to prosperity-Fed's Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Free markets best route to prosperity-Fed's Jordan.

text.p: Rules that enhance the functioning of markets do more to foster prosperity than political institutions, Cleveland Federal Reserve President Jerry Jordan said on Thursday.

Days before Fed policy makers are scheduled to meet, Jordan said he would not comment on recent economic data or inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy. Instead, his address to a conference sponsored by The Cato Institute, a conservative think-tank, focused on broad historical themes.
Jordan said the 20th century featured contests of ideas in the arenas of politics and economics.
In politics, the conflict was between dicatorship and democracy, he said. In economics, the competition was between centrally controlled economies and free markets.
"The contest is over," Jordan noted. In the 21st century, democracy and markets will prevail, he said.
"We may be entering the golden age of capitalism ... One lesson nobody can miss is that political organizations affect prosperity," Jordan said. "Some enhance prosperity and some hinder it."
Jordan said the successful public policies are those that enhance the effectiveness of markets.
He said those policies include deregulation, denationalisation (privatisation), tax-reform and tax-reduction.
"The relative size of the government sector is shrinking everywhere in the world," Jordan said.
Jordan said the job of central banks is to pursue sound money. When the value of money remains stable, it ensures that resources will not be wasted and encourages savings and investment, Jordan said.

In an inflation-prone environment, businessmen try to protect profits by raising prices, Jordan said. In a stable money environment, businessmen focus on increasing efficiency and productivity, he said.
Queried about the impact of electronic money, Jordan said that central banks can stabilise the value of money even when it is issued by private agencies rather than the government.
